result:
**REST:** simple, cacheable, tooling everywhere. HTTP caching (CDN, ETag) works out of the box, status codes and verbs are well understood, easy to debug with curl, easy rate-limit/auth per endpoint. Costs: over-fetching/under-fetching → multiple round trips or bloated payloads; endpoint sprawl as clients diverge; versioning is manual.

**GraphQL:** client picks exact fields, one request for nested data, strongly typed schema → codegen, introspection, and easy evolution via deprecation instead of versions. Great for many client types (web/mobile) with differing data needs. Costs: HTTP caching mostly lost (single POST endpoint; needs persisted queries or client cache); N+1 resolver problem (needs DataLoader); query-cost/depth limiting required or clients can DoS you; per-field authorization is harder; file uploads, error handling (200 with `errors`), and observability are clunkier; steeper learning curve.

**Verdict:** default to REST for a new API with few clients, public/cacheable resources, or a small team. Pick GraphQL when you have multiple frontends with diverging data needs, deeply nested/relational data, or want a federated gateway over many services. Don't pick it just for fashion; the operational overhead is real.
